page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this arm64 processor features 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per core, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The server achieves top-decile results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark memory scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached read and write operations. Database performance is similarly strong, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations reaching top-tier thresholds. However, single-core performance remains moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and text processing benchmarks placing in the middle 50%.

While multi-threaded execution and memory throughput are highly competitive, single-threaded tasks and certain LLM workloads present distinct tradeoffs. For instance, LLM text generation using a small 135M model falls into the bottom 10%, whereas text generation with larger 7B and 70B models performs in the top 25%. Given the 768.0 GB DDR5 memory capacity, 5700 GB local NVMe SSD storage, and high multi-core efficiency, this server is configured for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, static web serving, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server utilizing 96 dedicated physical cores of the 2.8 GHz AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high database operation speeds, though single-core processing and small-model LLM text generation show average to poor performance. This hardware profile delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads by combining high-density DDR5 RAM with local NVMe storage. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
